probes.reference: Viterbi decoding uses dynamic programming to find the most likely sequence.
probes.student: The algorithm finds the best state sequence by storing the optimal previous state at every step.
probes.note: Example from the Week 3 brief: same idea, few shared words.

probes.reference: Viterbi decoding uses dynamic programming to find the most likely sequence.
probes.student: Viterbi decoding greedily picks the most likely state at each step independently to find the sequence.
probes.note: Describes greedy decoding (the Week 1 motivating error) while reusing the reference vocabulary.

probes.reference: TF-IDF weights a word by its term frequency multiplied by its inverse document frequency; words such as 'the' that appear in most documents are down-weighted, while rare, discriminative words receive a higher weight.
probes.student: Words found in nearly every text carry little information, so their importance is pushed towards zero, while terms specific to a few texts are emphasised.

probes.reference: TF-IDF weights a word by its term frequency multiplied by its inverse document frequency; words such as 'the' that appear in most documents are down-weighted, while rare, discriminative words receive a higher weight.
probes.student: TF-IDF gives the highest weight to words that appear in most documents, because the inverse document frequency grows with the document frequency.
probes.note: All the right concepts, relationship inverted.

probes.reference: TF-IDF weights a word by its term frequency multiplied by its inverse document frequency; words such as 'the' that appear in most documents are down-weighted, while rare, discriminative words receive a higher weight.
probes.student: TF-IDF is a very important technique in NLP and is used in many applications to get good results.

probes.reference: Cosine similarity is the dot product of two vectors divided by the product of their norms; it depends only on direction, so it is insensitive to document length, unlike Euclidean distance.
probes.student: It looks at the angle between the two document vectors rather than how far apart their tips are, so a long and a short document on the same subject still come out close.

probes.reference: Cosine similarity is the dot product of two vectors divided by the product of their norms; it depends only on direction, so it is insensitive to document length, unlike Euclidean distance.
probes.student: In trigonometry the cosine of an angle is the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse of a right triangle.

probes.reference: Cosine similarity is the dot product of two vectors divided by the product of their norms; it depends only on direction, so it is insensitive to document length, unlike Euclidean distance.
probes.student: Cosine similarity divides the Euclidean distance by the dot product, so it depends heavily on document length.
probes.note: Correct terms, wrong formula and wrong conclusion.

probes.reference: Maximum likelihood gives zero probability to bigrams never seen in training; add-one (Laplace) smoothing adds one to every count and the vocabulary size to the denominator so no probability is zero.
probes.student: If a word pair never showed up in the training text the model would call any sentence containing it impossible, so we pretend every pair was seen one extra time.

probes.reference: Maximum likelihood gives zero probability to bigrams never seen in training; add-one (Laplace) smoothing adds one to every count and the vocabulary size to the denominator so no probability is zero.
probes.student: Add-one smoothing adds one to the vocabulary size so that frequent bigrams get a higher probability than in maximum likelihood.
probes.note: Uses the terms, gets the mechanism and purpose wrong.

probes.reference: Perplexity is the inverse probability of the test text normalised by the number of words; a lower perplexity means a better language model.
probes.student: It is two raised to the per-token cross-entropy, so the less surprised the model is by held-out text, the smaller the value and the better the model.
